name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 15
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 15

criteria.description: Presence of multisystemic clinical features consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction including neurological and muscular symptoms
Demonstration of combined defects in multiple respiratory chain enzyme complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation complexes
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multisystemic clinical features plus biochemical evidence of combined respiratory chain defects and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.notes: Elevated blood lactate due to impaired oxidative phosphorylation

common.notes: Reduced muscle tone commonly observed in infancy
Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Hearing impairment due to cochlear or neural involvement

occasional.notes: Focal or generalized seizures may occur

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Combined deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem signal abnormalities
Muscle MRI may show fatty infiltration and atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complex subunits or assembly factors
other: Muscle biopsy with ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Stroke-like episodes with focal neurological deficits
Onset typically in childhood or adolescence
Acute or subacute painless central vision loss

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia in infancy
Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystem involvement including neurological and cardiac manifestations
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
